edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Κἂν σεμνύνωνται τοίνυν Ἰουδαῖοι τῇ περιτομῇ, χωρίσουσιν αὐτὴν οὐ μόνον τῆς Κόλχων καὶ Αἰγυπτίων περιτομῆς ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς Ἰσμαηλιτῶν Ἀράβων, καίτοι γε ἀπὸ τοῦ προπάτορος αὐτῶν Ἀβραὰμ τοῦ Ἰσμαὴλ γεγενημένου καὶ σὺν ἐκείνῳ περιτεμνομένου. λέγουσι δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι τὴν μὲν ὀκταήμερον περιτομὴν εἶναι τὴν προηγουμένην, τὴν δὲ μὴ τοιαύτην ἐκ περιστάσεως· καὶ τάχα διά τινα πολέμιον τῷ Ἰουδαίων ἔθνει ἄγγελον αὐτὴ ἐτελεῖτο, δυνάμενον μὲν σίνεσθαι τοὺς μὴ περιτεμνομένους αὐτῶν, ἀτονοῦντα δὲ ἐν τοῖς περιτεμνομένοις. ὅπερ φήσει τις δηλοῦσθαι ἐκ τῶν ἐν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ γεγραμμένων, ἐν οἷς ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸ μὲν τῆς ιπερτομῆς τοῦ Ἐλιάζαρ ἐνεργεῖν ἐδύνατο κατὰ Μωϋσέως, περιτμηθέντος δ᾿ αὐτοῦ οὐδὲν ἴσχυσε. καὶ τοιαῦτά γε μαθοῦσα ἡ „Σεπφώρα λαβοῦσα ψῆφον περιέτεμε“ τὸ παιδίον ἑαυτῆς, κατὰ μὲν τὰ κοινὰ τῶν ἀντιγράφων λέγειν ἀναγεγραμμένη τό· „ἔστη τὸ αἷμα τῆς περιτομῆς τοῦ παιδίου μου,“ κατὰ δὲ τὸ Ἑβραϊκὸν αὐτό· „νυμφίος αἱμάτων σύ μοι.“ ᾔδει γὰρ τὸν περὶ τοῦ τοιουδὶ ἀγγέλου λόγον, δυναμένου πρὸ τοῦ αἵματος καὶ παυομένου διὰ τὸ τῆς περιτομῆς αἷμα· ἐφ᾿ ᾧ καὶ ἐλέχθη αὐτῷ τό· „νυμφίος αἱμάτων σύ μοι.“ ἀλλὰ ταῦτα μὲν περιεργότερά πως εἶναι δοκοῦντα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τῶν πολλῶν ἀκοὴν παρακεκινδυνευμένως ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον λελέχθω, οἷς ἔτι ἓν ὡς Χριστιανῷ πρέπον προσθεὶς ἐπὶ τὰ ἑξῆς μεταβήσομαι. ἐδύνατο γὰρ οὗτος οἶμαι ὁ ἄγγελος κατὰ τῶν μὴ περιτεμνομένων ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἁπαξαπλῶς πάντων τῶν σεβόντων μόνον τὸν δημιουργὸν, καὶ ἐπὶ τοσοῦτόν γε ἐδύνατο, ὅσον οὐκ ἀνειλήφει σῶμα ὁ Ἰησοῦς. ὅτε δ᾿ ἀνείληφε, καὶ περιετέμνετο τὸ ἐκείνου σῶμα, καθῃρέθη πᾶσα ἡ κατὰ τῶν ἐν τῇ θεοσεβείᾳ ταύτῃ περιτεμνομένων δύναμις αὐτοῦ· ἀφάτῳ γὰρ θειότητι καθεῖλεν ἐκεῖνον ὁ Ἰησοῦς. διὸ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἀπείρηται περιτέμνεσθαι καὶ λέγεται αὐτοῖς· „ὅτι ἐὰν περιτέμνησθε, Χριστὸς οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς ὠφελήσει.“
pass_a_gloss: Even if Jews pride themselves (σεμνύνωνται) on circumcision, they will separate (χωρίσουσιν) it not only from the circumcision of Colchians and Egyptians but also from that of the Ishmaelite Arabs, although Ishmael was born (γεγενημένου) from their forefather (προπάτορος) Abraham and circumcised with him. Jews say the eight-day (ὀκταήμερον) circumcision is the principal/primary (προηγουμένην), the not-such from circumstance (ἐκ περιστάσεως); and perhaps (τάχα) it was performed because of some angel (ἄγγελον) hostile (πολέμιον) to the nation of Jews, able to harm (σίνεσθαι) those of them not circumcised, but powerless (ἀτονοῦντα) in the circumcised. Which someone will say is shown from things written in Exodus, in which the angel before the circumcision of Eliazar (Ἐλιάζαρ) was able to act (ἐνεργεῖν) against Moses, but when he was circumcised had no strength (ἴσχυσε). And having learned such things, 'Sepphora taking a pebble (ψῆφον) circumcised' her child, recorded (ἀναγεγραμμένη) according to the common copies (κοινὰ τῶν ἀντιγράφων) to say 'the blood of the circumcision of my child stood/stopped (ἔστη)', but according to the Hebrew (Ἑβραϊκόν) itself 'bridegroom (νυμφίος) of bloods you to me'. For she knew the account (λόγον) about such an angel, having power before the blood and ceasing (παυομένου) because of the blood of circumcision; for which also was said to him 'bridegroom of bloods you to me'. But let these things, seeming somewhat over-curious (περιεργότερα) and not according to the hearing of the many, be said venturously (παρακεκινδυνευμένως) thus far; to which adding yet one thing fitting (πρέπον) as for a Christian, I shall pass to what follows. For this angel, I think (οἶμαι), had power against those of the people (λαοῦ) not circumcised and, in a word (ἁπαξαπλῶς), all those worshipping (σεβόντων) only the Creator (δημιουργόν), and had power so far as Jesus had not taken up (ἀνειλήφει) a body (σῶμα). But when he had taken it up, and his body was circumcised, all his power against those circumcised in this godliness (θεοσεβείᾳ) was taken down (καθῃρέθη); for by ineffable divinity (ἀφάτῳ θειότητι) Jesus took him down (καθεῖλεν). Therefore to his disciples it is forbidden (ἀπείρηται) to be circumcised, and it is said to them: 'that if you are circumcised Christ will profit (ὠφελήσει) you nothing.'

pass_b_english: So if the Jews do take pride in circumcision, they will distinguish it not only from the circumcision of the Colchians and Egyptians but also from that of the Ishmaelite Arabs, although Ishmael was born of their forefather Abraham and was circumcised together with him (Genesis 17:23–26). The Jews say that circumcision on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12) is the principal kind, and that circumcision not done in this way comes from force of circumstance.

And perhaps circumcision was performed because of some angel hostile to the Jewish nation, who was able to harm those of them who were not circumcised but was powerless against those who were. Someone will say that this is shown by what is written in Exodus, where before the circumcision of Eliezer the angel was able to act against Moses, but once Eliezer had been circumcised he could do nothing (Exodus 4:24–26). And having learned such things, “Zipporah took a pebble and circumcised” her child (Exodus 4:25). According to the common copies she is recorded as saying, “The blood of my child's circumcision has stopped” (Exodus 4:25–26), but according to the Hebrew, “You are a bridegroom of blood to me” (Exodus 4:25). For she knew the account of this sort of angel, who had power before the blood but ceased because of the blood of circumcision; and for this reason it was said to him, “You are a bridegroom of blood to me.”

But let this much be said, at some risk, about these matters, which seem rather over-curious and not suited to the ears of most people. To them I shall add one more point, as befits a Christian, and then pass on to what follows. For this angel, I think, had power against the uncircumcised among the people, and in a word among all who worshipped the Creator alone; and he had that power for as long as Jesus had not taken a body. But when Jesus had taken one, and His body was circumcised (Luke 2:21), all the angel's power against those circumcised in this worship of God was overthrown; for Jesus brought him down by His unspeakable divinity. That is why His disciples are forbidden to be circumcised, and it is said to them, “If you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing” (Galatians 5:2).
notes: Source typo ιπερτομῆς read as περιτομῆς. Exodus 4 does not name the son; Origen identifies him as Eliezer (Ἐλιάζαρ in this text; cf. Exodus 18:4), and LXX Exodus 4:24 has 'an angel of the Lord' where the Hebrew has the Lord; 'once Eliezer had been circumcised' clarifies the Greek 'he'. 'Zipporah took a pebble' matches LXX Exodus 4:25 (λαβοῦσα Σεπφωρα ψῆφον περιέτεμεν), which has 'the foreskin of her son' where Origen has 'her child'. The 'common copies' reading ἔστη τὸ αἷμα τῆς περιτομῆς τοῦ παιδίου μου is the LXX of Exodus 4:25 and 4:26; ἔστη taken as 'has stopped' (stanched). The Hebrew 'bridegroom of blood' is Exodus 4:25 (Hebrew; also 4:26). 'Said to him' is ambiguous in the Greek (the angel or Moses); kept ambiguous. Doubtful sense: 'all his power against those circumcised in this worship of God' translates the transmitted περιτεμνομένων; the argument might seem to want 'uncircumcised', but the text as given is translated without emendation. 'His' in 'His unspeakable divinity' added for English sense (ἀφάτῳ θειότητι). Galatians 5:2 quoted closely (Origen adds ὅτι). κατὰ τῶν μὴ περιτεμνομένων ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἁπαξαπλῶς πάντων τῶν σεβόντων: πάντων τῶν σεβόντων taken with ἀπό, parallel to τοῦ λαοῦ, so the angel's power is over the uncircumcised among all worshippers of the Creator (not over all such worshippers); this fits the claim that he was powerless against the circumcised. κἄν at the start of the chapter read as 'if' (the Jews do take pride), not concessive.

Open doubt (review): 5.48: the Greek has περιτεμνομένων in 'all his power against those circumcised in this worship of God was overthrown', and the argument might seem to want the uncircumcised. The text is translated as given, without emendation, and the translator note says so. Another edition should be checked if one is available.
